topic: How AI Actually Impacts Developer Workflows: JetBrains April 2026 Research

Analyzed 151,904,543 logged events for behavioral vs self-reported data comparison
AI redistributes and reshapes workflows in ways that elude developers' own perceptions
74% of AI-assisted developers didn't notice increased window switching, but telemetry confirmed it
AI users produce more code but also delete significantly more
Presented at ICSE 2026 in Rio de Janeiro, April 2026
Academic paper: Evolving with AI: A Longitudinal Analysis of Developer Logs
Dataset spans October 2022 to October 2024 across all devices
62 developers completed follow-up survey and interviews

stats.fact: JetBrains HAX team analyzed 151,904,543 logged events from 800 developers over 2 years (Oct 2022–Oct 2024) to study AI workflow impact
74% of AI-assisted developers did NOT notice an increase in window switching, yet telemetry on 151M IDE events confirmed AI users' switching trended upward over 2 years
85% of developers regularly use AI tools for coding and development in 2026
Only 18% of developers regularly use AI coding tools in their daily work despite 76% awareness of GitHub Copilot
Top benefits reported: increased productivity (74%), faster repetitive tasks (73%), less time searching for info (72%), faster coding (69%), faster learning (65%)
90% of developers using AI save at least one hour per week; 20% save eight or more hours
Developers complete tasks 55% faster when using GitHub Copilot, based on research involving 4,800 developers
GitHub Copilot generates an average of 46% of code written by users, with code acceptance rates of 27–30%
51% of all code committed to GitHub in early 2026 was either generated or substantially AI-assisted
73% of engineering teams use AI coding tools daily in 2026, up from 41% in 2025
Multi-agent workflow inquiries surged 1,445% in early 2026; coding agent sessions grew from avg 4 to 23 minutes
78% of agent coding sessions now involve multi-file edits, indicating more complex AI-assisted tasks
Developers actually take 19% longer to complete issues with AI (vs expected 24% faster), yet still perceived it as 20% faster — per METR study
Time spent on code review increased 12% when developers don't adequately verify AI-generated code; bug density 23% higher in unreviewed AI-generated code
stats.source: McKinsey survey of 4,500+ developers across 150 enterprises

stats.fact: 45% of developers say debugging AI-generated code is more time-consuming than writing it manually
GitHub Copilot has 4.7 million paid subscribers (up ~75% YoY) and ~20 million total users
